findings.reason: the author should either populate `see_also` (or explain in §11 why a populated-in-shortlist field cannot carry the siblings) or state that the field is dead and being retired, rather than silently adding a competing vocabulary for cross-IDS siblings.
findings.text: `SearchHit.see_also` is declared "Cross-IDS sibling paths from shared semantic clusters", the exact concept §11 introduces; it is never populated by any producer (`hybrid_dd_search` builds `SearchHit` at dd_search.py:369 without it and no other site sets it), and the only reader is `imas_codex/llm/search_formatters.py:1212`. §11 instead invents a second vocabulary, `arms = cluster:<seed path>`, on the `Candidate` that composes that very `SearchHit`

findings.reason: the write path names the whole file, so "removed with it" reads as deleting coverage for a helper two reused search functions depend on; §8 must name the single class to drop and keep the rest.
findings.text: §8 says "The test of that arm's DD-version filter in `tests/tools/test_dd_version_filtering.py` is removed with it", but the file also holds `TestDDVersionClause` (9 tests of `_dd_version_clause`), `TestClusterScopeQuery`, `TestOverviewQueryStructure`, `TestExportQueryStructure`, `TestListPathsQuery` and `TestClusterReranking` — and `_dd_version_clause` is the shared filter `hybrid_dd_search` (§4) and `related_dd_search` (§11) both call; only `TestSemanticMatchDDVersion` (:436) is arm-specific

findings.reason: the section must name what the `TargetType` classmethod retires or merges, or state why nothing can be, so the added public-definition surface is accounted for as the rubric requires.
findings.text: with this week's `public_definitions` at 0, §8 adds three public definitions — `read_candidates` and `select_candidates` (graph_ops.py), and a classmethod on `TargetType` (:44) — while naming only two retirements in that family (`count_sources_by_mapping_status` workers.py:434 and the workers.py `count_candidates_by_route` :419); §8's other retirements are three SignalSource fields and two CLI options (both already removed by edge-ownership, eb75bb0ab, so they offset nothing new)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_codex/ids/candidates.py` is one deep module hiding embedding, per-IDS arm merge, IDS routing, batched pair judgment and routing behind five functions; §11 adds its expansion beside `retrieve_candidates` in the same module rather than spreading wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names the owners it consolidates: `count_candidates_by_route` is a live duplicate (`imas_codex/ids/workers.py:419` and `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:653`, functionally identical queries) and §8 deletes the workers.py copy and repoints `discover status`/`clear`; the `MAPS_TO_IMAS` create/delete census now resolves to `graph_ops.py:585`/`:640` as the plan states.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 adds public definitions without naming an offsetting retirement in that family (below).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §8/§11 reuse `hybrid_dd_search`, `related_dd_search` (dd_search.py:606, verified to return cross-IDS cluster siblings exactly as claimed), `call_decisions`, `PipelineCost`, `candidate_worker`/`claim_batch` and the `_candidate_record`/`CandidateWriteError` check; but one existing home for the §11 concept is left unused (below), and §8 removes a shared-filter test file.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `read_candidates`/`select_candidates` are not thin wrappers: the plan justifies `select_candidates` as a distinct function because `write_candidates` (graph_ops.py:464) deletes and rewrites every edge of a source while a pick must flag existing edges without disturbing the shortlist.
